title: In vitro degradation and biocompatibility evaluation of typical biodegradable metals (Mg/Zn/Fe) for the application of tracheobronchial stenosis

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: A paediatric tracheobronchial stent must hold the airway for 3-12 months and then vanish; permanent stents provoke granulation. Degradation of the candidate biodegradable metals has never been assessed in an airway fluid or against airway epithelium.
states.detail: Absorbed: b1 (HYP/need), b2 (HYP/gap), b3 (HYP/hypothesis), b4 (DES/base_system), b5 (DES/variable_sweep), b6 (DES/method), b7 (PRC/forming), b8 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: A paediatric airway stent has to support the lumen for 3-12 months

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Corrosion layers are carbonate plus phosphate; the GS layers on Mg and Zn carry far less P and Ca than the SBF layers. HP-Mg attack spreads over the whole surface within 14 d, while HP-Zn and P-Fe stay largely localised

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: 28-d corrosion rate in GS is well below SBF: 0.78 vs 2.01 (Mg), 0.03 vs 0.10 (Zn), 0.09 vs 0.13 mm/y (Fe). HP-Mg is ~240 mV nobler and carries ~12x lower corrosion current in GS than in SBF; Zn and Fe differ little between media.
states.detail: Absorbed: b11 (PRP/value), b12 (PRP/value), b13 (PRP/value), b15 (MEC/pathway), b16 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Porcine stomach mucin co-precipitates with phosphate and strongly suppresses phosphate deposition; SBF holds about 1.3x the chloride of GS and far less bicarbonate (Table 2)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: HP-Mg and HP-Zn degrade slowly enough and remain benign enough for a temporary airway stent; P-Fe is disqualified by its A549 toxicity

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: In an airway-simulating fluid HP-Zn and HP-Mg are the viable degradable tracheobronchial stent metals, and SBF overstates their degradation

nodes.solves: HP-Mg attack spreads over the whole surface within 14 d, while HP-Zn and P-Fe stay largely localised

nodes.title: ASSAY, F4
nodes.head: GS starts at pH 8.0-8.4 for every metal and settles to ~7.0 by 28 d, while SBF holds 7.2-7.5 throughout; no trace rises above 8.5
nodes.solves: GS mucin suppresses phosphate deposition but its low chloride and bicarbonate buffering limit pitting and hold the pH near neutral, so Mg corrodes slower than in SBF
nodes.note: day-to-day scatter is ~0.3 pH units in all three panels, and GS ends below SBF rather than above it

use: On the $7 \mathrm { d }$ , for samples immersed in GS, the most severe corrosion happened in $\mathrm { H P - M g }$ (Fig. 2(a)A), which started at discrete sites, and expanded to cover the whole specimen on 14 d (Fig. 2(b)A).
The corrosion of $\mathrm { H P - M g }$ immersed in SBF even got worse with nearly complete corroded surface on 7 d (Fig. 2(a)B).

On the $7 \mathrm { d }$ , for samples immersed in GS, the most severe corrosion happened in $\mathrm { H P - M g }$ (Fig. 2(a)A), which started at discrete sites, and expanded to cover the whole specimen on 14 d (Fig. 2(b)A).
Inversely, the corrosion area on HP-Zn and P-Fe was still at discrete sites even on $^ { 1 4 \mathrm { d } }$ in SBF (Fig. 2(b)D and Fig. 2(b)F).

use: In contrast, higher cathodic corrosion potential value and lower corrosion current density (Fig. 1(c)) were observed for $\mathrm { H P - M g }$ immersed in GS than in SBF, indicting the GS electrolyte solution had more moderate corrosion property for HP-Mg.

And the calculated corrosion rates after 28-day immersion (Fig. 3(c)) in GS were only $0 . 7 8 \mathrm { m m / y }$ , $0 . 0 3 4 \mathrm { m m } / \mathrm { y }$ and $0 . 1 0 2 \mathrm { m m } / \mathrm { y }$ for HP-Mg, HP-Zn and P-Fe, respectively, which were lower than SBF group $( 2 . 0 1 \mathrm { m m } / \mathrm { y }$ in HPMg, $0 . 1 0 2 \mathrm { m m } / \mathrm { y }$ in $\mathrm { H P - } Z \mathrm { n }$ and $0 . 1 3 6 \mathrm { m m } / \mathrm { y }$ in P-Fe).
The cytotoxicity test (Fig. 6(b)) revealed that at day 1, P-Fe-IC had the strongest cytotoxicity compared with the negative group.

As for the difference between cell morphology (Fig. 5(j)) and cytotoxicity test results (Fig. 6(b)) for HPMg in DC group, the cells on the bottom of the culture plates may be the main reason to cause higher absorbance value.
